The diagram above shows a unit circle and the angle $\theta $ measured in the usual way. Given that the $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $-0.26,$ calculate the reference angle ${\theta }_{R}$ to the nearest integer.

${\theta }_{R}≈$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
question.worked_solution:
The reference angle is the acute angle that $\theta $ makes with the $x$-axis.

First, we create a right-triangle by drawing a vertical line from $P$ to the $x$-axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225277/assets/403edda1121bb4a647a52fcff755659ab1f9fe2ea310572b13be423cef4d6db9.png)

So, we have the following triangle, where ${\theta }_{R}$ is the reference angle of $\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225277/assets/38a60a712b18a4b9575ed812f8bd184a56ae5969fe865b9edc12f2b0faccd48f.png)

We know that the hypotenuse has a length of $1$ because it is a radius of the unit circle. 

Now, using the triangle above, we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡{\theta }_{R}=\frac{0.26}{1}=0.26.
$$

Now, we compute the angle ${\theta }_{R}$ using the inverse cosine:

$$
{\theta }_{R}=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(0.26)≈{75}^{∘}
$$
